# TrendChart

<!-- Generated by js/scripts/widget-pages.mjs from the trait contract: edit the schema
     or the script, then run it again. -->

Trend of named pens against wall-clock time, live or browsing the history (IND-070 .. IND-075).

![TrendChart, dark theme](../img/widgets/trend-chart-dark.png#only-dark){ width="528" }

schema [`trendchart.schema.json`](../trait-contract.md)

## Example

The traits of the picture above:

```python
ai.TrendChart(
    label="TrendChart",
    pens=[
        {
            "name": "LT-101",
            "unit": "m",
            "min": 0,
            "max": 4,
            "hi": 3,
            "hihi": 3.5,
            "setpoint": 2.2,
        },
        {"name": "FT-101", "unit": "L/s", "min": 0, "max": 60},
    ],
    history=1000,
    size=(520, 220),
)
```

The data of the picture (samples, history or drawing) is sent with the widget's methods,
not as traits: see the [widget catalog](../widgets.md).

## Traits

| Trait | Type | Default | Set by | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | array | `[560,260]` | host | [width, height] in CSS pixels. |
| `value` | object | `{}` | host | Latest value of each pen, by pen name, written by the host with each append. |
| `pens` | array of object | `[]` | host | Pens {name, unit, min, max, color, lolo, lo, hi, hihi, setpoint, format}. Python normalizes them (a string is a pen name, missing keys get their defaults) and rejects duplicate names, unknown keys and max <= min; the front end shows an invalid scale as 0 .. 100. |
| `span` | number | `600` | host, widget | Seconds shown; set by the operator with the span selector. |
| `history` | integer | `10000` | host | Samples kept per pen (IND-074). |
